chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her brother and on behalf of her sister. And he said: The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her son.
ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of her brother or son?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi confirms the permissibility of a woman performing Hajj on behalf of male relatives, specifically her brother, sister, and son, reflecting the Shia juristic view that gender does not restrict the validity of proxy pilgrimage. It highlights the practical application of 'Hajj al-Badal' in cases where the principal is unable to perform the ritual due to age, illness, or other impediments. The narration underscores the familial duty and spiritual continuity within the household as interpreted by Imam al-Sadiq.
